failure_modes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 3 solver summary states 'The claim that an MTV show called "You Can't See Me" was hosted by a member of Likwit Crew (Defari's band) cannot be verified from the provided passages. The passages contain no mention of Defari, the Likwit Crew, or any MTV show with the title "You Can't See Me."' However, the hop 3 passages explicitly include: (1) 'Likwit Crew | The Likwit Crew is a West Coast hip hop collective...artists such as Xzibit, Phil Da Agony, Lootpack, Defari...' (2) 'Street Music | Street Music is the third album by Defari, an American hip hop musician who is also part of the Likwit Crew' (3) 'IV Life | ...The production on this album is sample reliant and artists sampled include A Tribe Called Quest (on "You Can't See Me")...' The solver claims these entities are not mentioned when they explicitly appear in the retrieved passages.

failure_modes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
failure_modes.evidence: The hop 3 passages contain the critical link: 'IV Life | IV Life is the fourth album by West Coast hip hop artist King Tee...artists sampled include A Tribe Called Quest (on "You Can't See Me")'. Combined with 'Likwit Crew | ...founded by King T[ee] who recruited Tha Alkaholiks...artists such as Xzibit, Phil Da Agony, Lootpack, Defari...' and 'Street Music | ...Defari, an American hip hop musician who is also part of the Likwit Crew', the passages establish that King Tee (founder/member of Likwit Crew, which includes Defari) has a track titled 'You Can't See Me' on his album IV Life. The solver claims this evidence is absent when it is present.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Who hosted the MTV show "You Can't See Me" and were they a member of Likwit Crew?' This is a natural-language yes/no question bundling multiple targets (show host identity + Likwit Crew membership verification) in a form poorly suited for entity-based retrieval systems.

failure_modes.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
failure_modes.evidence: The claim states 'The MTV show that was hosted by a member of this band...was You Can't See Me.' The hop 3 passage shows 'You Can't See Me' is a track title on King Tee's album IV Life (sampling A Tribe Called Quest), not an MTV show. King Tee is a Likwit Crew member/founder. The solver should have identified that 'You Can't See Me' is mischaracterized as an MTV show in the claim when the evidence shows it is a song title, constituting a factual error in the claim. Instead, the solver claims the evidence is missing rather than recognizing the category error.
